entities.name: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake, also known as the Sumatran earthquake, occurred on December 26, 2004, at 00:58:53 UTC with a magnitude of 9.1–9.3. It is the third-largest earthquake in recorded history and is considered one of the most significant natural disasters of the 21st century.

This megathrust earthquake and subsequent tsunami caused widespread destruction and loss of life across several countries in Southeast Asia and East Africa, including Indonesia, Thailand, Sri Lanka, and Myanmar. The tsunami waves reached as high as 30 meters in some areas, affecting coastal communities and causing catastrophic damage to infrastructure and the environment.

The impact of the earthquake and tsunami was felt globally, with international aid and relief efforts mobilized to support the affected regions. The disaster led to significant changes in disaster preparedness and response, including the establishment of the Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System.

The 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami serves as a poignant reminder of the power of nature and the importance of disaster preparedness and response. As noted by the United Nations, 'The tsunami was a devastating reminder of the importance of disaster risk reduction and management.'

One of the most striking statistics to emerge from the disaster is the estimated 230,000 people who lost their lives, making it one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history.
